newsitem.title: UK: UK decides not to refer East Midlands buy to MMC.
newsitem.headline: UK decides not to refer East Midlands buy to MMC.

text.p: The UK's secretary of state for trade and industry said on Wednesday he would not refer the proposed buy of East Midlands Electricity by DR Investments (UK) Plc, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources Inc, to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).

Ian Lang said in a statement the decision was in line with his general approach to mergers involving regional electricity companies, which was based primarily on whether a merger should be referred on competition grounds.

"I also looked at whether there were other public interest issues raised by the bid. I agreed with the DGFT (director general of fair trading) and DGES (director general of electricity supply) that there were no concerns warranting reference to the MMC," he added.
He said DR Investments had given assurances to address regulatory concerns.
Dominion said earlier this week that it had won acceptances representing 32.8 percent of East Midlands Electricity following its $2.15 billion agreed bid.
Analysts had expected the bid to get approval from the UK authorities after CE Electric's hostile bid for regional electricity company Northern Electric was given the go-ahead on December 13.
